stem: When coordinating post-transplant psychological care, which monitoring priority aligns with standard references?

options.text: Monitor the patient for signs of depression and anxiety
Psychological health requires no follow-up after hospital discharge
Depression screening applies only to living donors, not recipients
Anxiety is expected and should never be discussed with the team

explanation.rationale_correct: Psychological care teaching notes that psychological health after transplant is as important as physical health and includes monitoring for signs of depression and anxiety.

rationale_incorrect.B: Ongoing psychological monitoring is part of post-transplant care rather than being deferred indefinitely.
rationale_incorrect.C: Recipient psychological health is specifically addressed in post-transplant teaching.
rationale_incorrect.D: Open monitoring and support for depression and anxiety are encouraged rather than avoiding discussion.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → f. Psychological care → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Monitor patient for signs of depression and anxiety

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → f. Psychological care → ii. (monitor for depression and anxiety); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Recipient psychological-monitoring angle distinct from living-donor depression/anxiety teaching (cctc-1023, p. 341) and appearance/body-image counseling (cctc-1124); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: When teaching health maintenance after transplantation, which household vaccination counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Caregivers, family members, and co-workers should receive annual influenza vaccinations unless otherwise contraindicated
Only transplant recipients need influenza vaccination; household contacts are exempt
Household members should receive live influenza vaccine to protect the recipient
Influenza vaccination is discouraged for all household contacts

explanation.rationale_correct: Health maintenance teaching includes annual inactivated influenza vaccine for recipients and notes that caregivers, family members, and co-workers should also receive annual influenza vaccinations unless contraindicated.

rationale_incorrect.B: Household and caregiver influenza vaccination is specifically recommended to reduce exposure risk.
rationale_incorrect.C: Recipients should receive inactivated influenza vaccine rather than live formulations.
rationale_incorrect.D: Household influenza vaccination is encouraged rather than discouraged.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: caregivers, family members, and co-workers receive annual influenza vaccinations unless otherwise contraindicated

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Health maintenance → ii. (caregiver/family/co-worker annual influenza vaccination); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Household influenza-vaccination angle distinct from inactivated-recipient vaccine combo (cctc-1048) and meningococcal high-risk groups (cctc-1090); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A kidney recipient who enjoys gardening asks about infection-prevention precautions while working in soil. Which teaching point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Wear gloves and a mask for garden activity or working in dirt
Gardening is permanently contraindicated for all transplant recipients
Bare-hand contact with soil is preferred to maintain immunity
Masks are required only in hospital settings, never at home outdoors

explanation.rationale_correct: Infection-prevention teaching for other exposures includes wearing gloves and a mask for garden activity or working in dirt, along with cleaning and covering recent cuts or wounds.

rationale_incorrect.B: Gardening may continue with precautions rather than being universally prohibited.
rationale_incorrect.C: Gloves and mask are recommended for soil exposure rather than bare-hand contact.
rationale_incorrect.D: Mask use is cited for garden and dirt exposure at home as well as other infection-prevention settings.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → vi. Others
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Wear gloves and mask for garden activity or working in dirt

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).

notes: Source-first item. Garden/dirt exposure angle distinct from cat-litter/animal-safety combo (cctc-1116) and hand-hygiene teaching (cctc-1019); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A coordinator is updating post-transplant health-maintenance teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: The patient should be monitored for signs of depression and anxiety.
Caregivers, family members, and co-workers should receive annual influenza vaccinations unless otherwise contraindicated.
Immunosuppressed patients should routinely receive live-virus vaccines after transplantation.
Pneumococcal vaccine should be given ≥8 weeks after transplant.

explanation.rationale_correct: Psychological monitoring, household influenza vaccination, and pneumococcal vaccination timing are supported. Statement III is false because immunosuppressed patients should not receive live-virus vaccines.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—pneumococcal vaccine is recommended ≥8 weeks after transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because live-virus vaccines are contraindicated after transplantation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → f. Psychological care and g. Health maintenance
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Monitor patient for signs of depression and anxiety … caregivers, family members, and co-workers receive annual influenza vaccinations … Pneumococcal vaccine ≥8 weeks after transplant … should not receive live-virus vaccines

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → f. Psychological care → ii. and g. Health maintenance → ii. (depression/anxiety monitoring, household influenza, pneumococcal timing, live-vaccine contraindication); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Health-maintenance/psychological combo distinct from vaccination combo (cctc-1048) and return-to-work combo (cctc-1133); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.
